subject: Production: Hosted API latency spike — customer escalation & comms
body_1:
From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@acme-cloud.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: sarah.tan@brightapps.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spike affecting inference API (p95/p99 elevated)

Jordan —

We started seeing sustained p95/p99 increases across several critical routes hitting our service tier around 08:40 PT this morning. Error rate also ticked up on few tails (504s) and throughput throttles observed by our load testing gave backend 429s intermittently. This is affecting inference endpoints we use for feature extraction in our recommender.

Attached is a short CSV with sample request ids and timings (latency-sample-20261103.csv). We are currently paged. Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood Hosted API incident or a client-side spike?

Impact: production traffic degraded with measurable user impact (latency saw p99 ~ 2.6s vs baseline ~ 700ms).

Need: quick confirmation, ETA for mitigation, and an incident contact.

Thanks,
Tom Harris
Engineering Manager — ACME Cloud

---
Attachment: latency-sample-20261103.csv (text/csv, 18KB)

body_3:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, tom.harris@acme-cloud.com
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:05:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike affecting inference API (p95/p99 elevated)

Tom/Jordan —

Preliminary triage notes (initial 20m):
- We see an increase in p95/p99 on the hosted inference tier in us-west-2 starting ~08:36 PT.
- Error spikes correlate with larger-context requests (seq_len > 1024) and sustained high concurrency from a small set of customers.
- KV cache hit rate dropped on several shards (see attached heatmap: kv-cache-heatmap.png). Early hypothesis: cache thrash from concurrent prefix patterns causing more work per request and hitting a slow path in the runtime kernel selection.
- No throttling config changes from our side in the last 24h. Autoscaler reports elevated queue lengths for a subset of pools.

Immediate actions started:
- Rolled a high-priority config to increase concurrency headroom on the affected pool (temporary).
- Enabled detailed per-request tracing for sampled traffic; link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/latency/20261103-analysis
- Captured heap and runtime profiles for 09:00–09:20 window (heap-profiles-20261103.tar.gz attached).

We will follow up with an incident number and an interim ETA. Looks like this is hosted-side (runtime behavior + cache).

Neha Kapoor
Sr. SRE — Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv-cache-heatmap.png, heap-profiles-20261103.tar.gz

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: tom.harris@acme-cloud.com, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike affecting inference API (p95/p99 elevated) — follow-up & next steps

Tom/Jordan —

Follow-up from yesterday's incident: we contained the immediate spike within ~90 minutes by temporarily increasing pool headroom and deploying a kernel fallback that avoided the runtime slow path for large-context requests. Root cause (short): concurrent prefix patterns caused KV cache thrash on shared shards which pushed request handling into a slower execution path; combined with a surge in simultaneous large-context requests this produced the p95/p99 regressions and some 504s.

What we delivered:
- Incident containment: ~09:40 PT on 2026-11-03.
- Interim mitigation: increased pool headroom + kernel fallback.
- Customer comms: Status page posted, direct notes sent to affected accounts.
- Short-term operational work: adjust autoscaler thresholds and add per-customer concurrency caps for impacted pools.

Next steps (timeline):
- Week 1: permanent runtime fix to reduce cache thrash (engineering patch + canary)
- Week 2: publish guidance for large-context best practices and recommended batching patterns
- Week 3: automated detection and alerting for KV cache hit-rate drops + playbook

We will schedule a short postmortem and share a timeline for credit/SLAs if applicable. Jordan/Marissa — please coordinate ACME outreach; recommend offering a small credit and a one-on-one tech sync with Neha and our runtime team.

Monica Patel
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
